conviction_note: Scaled number = (2*0.60-1)*6.5 = +1.3: a lean long resting on company-level numbers (Q3 has never been below Q2 in 2023-2025 while the $68.5m consensus sits 2.8% below Q2's $70.5m; three straight beat-and-raise quarters each bought +3.8% to +7.8%), held at p_up 60 rather than higher because the seasonality read is an inference, Q3 carries most of the ~$10m set deployment (FCF optics), 7D capital is lumpy and the stock is +6% over 20 days into the print. The findings sum (+2.5) is larger than the scaled number because the beat and the raise findings each carry their own full size; they share one mechanism (a Q3 beat), which is why p_up is not higher.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $68.5m and non-GAAP EPS about -$0.21/-$0.22: MarketBeat earnings page (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/KIDS/earnings/, $68.50M, -$0.21) and Benzinga estimates (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/KIDS/earnings-forecasts, $68.5M, -$0.22, snippet_only, page 403 on fetch). Two sources agree on revenue. Company guide: FY2026 revenue $265.0-269.0m (raised Aug 4), adj EBITDA ~$25m, set deployment ~$10m, FCF breakeven (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001425450/000142545026000066/kidsq22026earningsrelease.htm). H1 2026 = $129.9m, so the guide implies H2 $135.1-139.1m; consensus Q3 $68.5m + Q4 $68.6m = FY $267.0m, the guide midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest 977,329 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement (published 2026-10-26), 5.55% of float, 4.8 days to cover, up 5.1% from 929,989 on 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/KIDS/short-interest; Equibles agrees at 4.80 days, ~3.7% of 26.11m shares outstanding: https://equibles.com/stocks/kids/short-interest). Moderate, not crowded. No usable skew: the baseline's option chain is unusable (ATM spread 170% of mid, total OI 73), so the market has made no directional statement. Tape: +6.02% over 20 days, +2.68% over 5 days, 8.9% below the 52-week high, after recovering from ~$21 where the 24% holder Squadron Capital finished selling on 2026-09-10.

findings.finding: The Q3 2026 revenue consensus of $68.5m sits 2.8% BELOW Q2 2026's reported $70.5m, yet Q3 revenue has been at or above Q2 in each of the last three years: 2023 $40.0m vs $39.6m, 2024 $54.6m vs $52.8m, 2025 $61.2m vs $61.1m (2025 despite delayed 7D capital sales); a merely flat sequential Q3 ($70.5m) would beat the bar by ~2.9%, and management called the summer surgery schedule encouraging.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have been bought: Q2 2026 beat $68.21m by 3.4% -> +6.85%; Q1 2026 beat $58.29m by 1.8% -> +3.78%; Q4 2025 beat $61.27m by 0.6% -> +7.76% (with the 2026 guide context). The one revenue miss (Q3 2025, $61.25m vs $63.63m, -3.7%) was pre-announced on 2025-10-09 and that day fell -9.19%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the street had priced normal summer seasonality, the Q3 consensus would sit at or above $70.5m rather than $2m below it; instead estimates were set just inside the guide's implied H2 run-rate ($67.5-69.5m a quarter). The stock's +6% 20-day run-up is modest and mostly the rebound from the Squadron block selling, not an estimate revision (consensus target moved $26.44 -> $26.50 in a month).
findings.independence: Prior-year Q2/Q3 figures from separate releases: Q3 2024 $54.6m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1425450/000142545024000090/kidsq32024earningsrelease.htm), Q2 2024 $52.8m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1425450/000142545024000077/kidsq22024earningsrelease.htm), Q3 2025 $61.2m (https://quantisnow.com/insight/orthopediatrics-corp-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results-6247758). Bar from MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/KIDS/earnings/). The seasonality is an inference from history, not a disclosed Q3 number.

findings.finding: Management has raised the FY2026 revenue guide at every print by roughly the size of the quarter's beat (Jan $262-266m -> Apr $263-267m -> Aug $265-269m), and the current FY consensus ($267.0m) sits exactly at the midpoint, so a Q3 beat of ~$2m on the pattern above would likely bring a fourth raise to around $267-271m, putting the guide above consensus for the first time this year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both 2026 raises (2026-04-30, 2026-08-04) were met with gains of +3.78% and +6.85%; the 2025-10-09 guide cut (to $233.5-234.5m) took -9.19%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Aug raise was described as still modestly below sell-side consensus (https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/orthopediatrics-corp-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-increases-2026-financial-guidance coverage), and FY consensus now equals the guide midpoint, so a raise beyond $269m top end is not in the numbers. If priced, Q4 consensus would sit above $69.5m (the guide's top-end implied quarter) rather than $68.6m.
findings.independence: Shares its mechanism with finding 1 (a Q3 beat is what funds the raise); counted separately because it lands on the guide line, but if finding 1 is wrong this one is too. Guide history from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001425450/000142545026000066/kidsq22026earningsrelease.htm).

findings.finding: No pre-announcement this October: EDGAR shows no 8-K from KIDS after the 2026-08-04 Q2 release (only Form 4s, a Form 144 and Squadron's 13D/As), whereas in 2025 the company pre-announced its Q3 revenue miss and cut the FY guide on 2025-10-09, three weeks before the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-09 pre-announced miss and guide cut: -9.19%; the 2025-10-28 print that followed: -2.66%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the market can see the absence too, and the 20-day run-up may reflect it. It lowers the odds of a large miss given this management's demonstrated practice of pre-releasing one, rather than adding upside.
findings.independence: 2025 precedent: https://quantisnow.com/insight/orthopediatrics-corp-announces-preliminary-third-quarter-2025-revenue-and-revised-6228891 . An absence-based inference, sized small for that reason.

findings.finding: Scoliosis (24% of revenue) fell 9% in Q2 2026 to $16.9m on the timing of 7D capital placements and Brazil stocking-distributor set sales, with underlying implant growth stated as mid-teens, and Q3 2025 is an easy comp because its revenue was depressed by delayed 7D capital sales; a return of deferred 7D placements would add to Q3, while trauma & deformity (75%, +26% in Q2) carries the rest.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025, when 7D capital delays caused the miss, took -9.19% on the pre-announcement; Q2 2026, when scoliosis fell 9% but T&D grew 26%, still rose +6.85%, so the market looked through the segment when the total beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $68.5m does not assume a 7D catch-up (it is below Q2); if the street expected deferred placements to land, the Q3 number would be above Q2. Lumpy capital equipment cuts both ways, hence the wide band.
findings.independence: Q2 release segment table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001425450/000142545026000066/kidsq22026earningsrelease.htm) and Q3 2025 pre-announcement citing delayed 7D capital sales (https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/orthopediatrics-preliminary-q3-revenue-61-2m-consensus-63-63m-thefly). Net of the rest: T&D at 75% of revenue growing 20%+ is what carries the total; this finding is only the swing segment.

findings.finding: Most of the ~$10m 2026 set deployment was guided to fall in Q3, so Q3 free cash flow is likely negative even though management promised positive FCF for H2 and breakeven for the year; cash was $47.9m at June 30 against a $48.4m term loan and a $48.8m convertible note.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FCF has improved every quarter of 2026 (Q1 -$5.0m, Q2 -$3.1m) and the stock rose on both prints; no record of how it reacts to a sequential FCF step back.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside what the company guided (the set deployment timing was said on the call), so mostly priced; residual risk is a headline cash decline read without the timing context.
findings.independence: Cash and debt from the Q2 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001425450/000142545026000066/kidsq22026earningsrelease.htm . The Q3 timing of set deployment rests on one call summary.

findings.finding: HCA's Q3 2026 release (out this morning) shows same-facility inpatient surgeries -1.4% and outpatient surgeries -3.7% year on year, with rising uninsured volume from exchange coverage losses; this is roughly unchanged from Q2 2026 (-2.3% / -3.4%), a quarter in which KIDS grew revenue 15%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed link: KIDS beat in Q2 2026 while the same HCA series was negative.
findings.why_not_priced: Public this morning, so priced as a macro read; it is an adult-hospital proxy for a pediatric, largely Medicaid/CHIP-funded, trauma-heavy business, and transmission is unconfirmed by the company.
findings.independence: Proxy only. J&J's Q3 2026 10-Q shows orthopaedics +3.4% operational with trauma growth from launches (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000197/jnj-20260927.htm), which points the other way for trauma, so net this is near zero.

findings.finding: The 24% holder Squadron Capital filed a Form 144 for 700,000 shares on 2026-08-24 and had sold exactly that amount by 2026-09-10 (375,131 shares at $23.04-25.75 through Sep 1 per 13D/A No. 3, then 324,869 at $21.01-23.35 per 13D/A No. 4, 'to provide additional capital for its other portfolio businesses'); no new 144 has been filed since, and the stock has recovered from the $21.01 block price to $24.13.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The selling coincided with the stock falling from ~$26 (post-Q2 high) to ~$21; it has since recovered most of that.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the rebound to $24 already reflects a finished seller. Kept small because it means no known block supply sits on the print day itself.
findings.independence: Form 144: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1425450/000142545026000079/primary_doc.xml ; 13D/A No. 3: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1425450/000119312526378878/primary_doc.xml . Same filer, one fact.

outside_window.finding: Squadron Capital (6.2m shares, 23.8%) sold 700k shares in the window after the Q2 print to fund other portfolio businesses; if the pattern repeats it would file a new Form 144 and resume selling a few weeks after the Q3 print, a supply overhang dated after the exit window.

baseline_tension: No usable skew exists to agree or disagree with; the long lean agrees with a modest +6% 20-day run-up that is mostly the rebound from finished block selling, so the run-up has not obviously pre-paid a beat.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (absence of a filing is not a cause): the no-pre-announcement finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3, since it rests on an absence, though kept because this management has a documented practice of pre-releasing a miss
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): bar confirmed on two agreeing estimate sources ($68.5m MarketBeat and Benzinga) plus the company guide, so no cap applied
Lesson 1 (reaction function veto): checked; this name has bought all three 2026 beats (+7.76, +3.78, +6.85), so the beat finding was left at full size
Last section (history built from wrong events): base rate rebuilt from confirmed prints, excluding the two pre-announcement dates; abs_move 6.5 left standing
Lessons 3 and 9: the beat and guidance findings' shared mechanism is stated in independence; the scoliosis finding was already sized net of T&D; no further change
